<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913794_theRebbe_460" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913794_theRebbe_460__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that for Rosh Hashanah, physical shofar blowing is required, encompassing both the straight ram's horn (representing self-nullification of all desires) and the bent ram's horn (representing the higher work of subjugation).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, not only is physical action required</t>
    <t s="2">(and the spiritual aspect of teshuvah is not sufficient, nor even the recitation of verses),</t>
    <t s="3">but within this itself, it is not sufficient that it be the inner voice of man; rather, one must specifically blow with the sound of a ram's horn of an animal,</t>
    <t s="4">[either] a straight ram's horn or bent ram's horns,</t>
    <t s="5">according to the two opinions in this matter, for these and those are the words of the living G-d.</t>
    <t s="6">And also now,</t>
    <t s="7">when we blow</t>
    <t s="8">(on Rosh Hashanah)</t>
    <t s="9">with bent ram's horns,</t>
    <t s="10">there are these two aspects in the spiritual service.</t>
    <t s="11">[The aspect] of a straight ram's horn, because "the more a person straightens his mind, the better,"</t>
    <t s="12">and it is explained in Chassidus</t>
    <t s="13">that this is that a person must strip himself of all his desires.</t>
    <t s="14">And the intention is not [only] for undesirable desires,</t>
    <t s="15">for what would that teach us?</t>
    <t s="16">And this matter</t>
    <t s="17">(that he should have no undesirable desires)</t>
    <t s="18">is already accomplished through the service of the month of Elul before Rosh Hashanah.</t>
    <t s="19">And the matter of "a person straightens his mind" on Rosh Hashanah is that he should strip himself of every [mental] image, even an image of holiness.</t>
    <t s="20">For the drawing down of Rosh Hashanah is from that which is beyond the category of place and beyond the category of image,</t>
    <t s="21">therefore the service of "straightening" [stripping] is required,</t>
    <t s="22">and through the simplicity [self-nullification] within man, he draws down the simplicity above,</t>
    <t s="23">even reaching the aspect of the ultimate simplicity.</t>
    <t s="24">And we blow with bent ram's horns, because "the more a person bends his mind, the better,"</t>
    <t s="25">and it is explained in Chassidus</t>
    <t s="26">that this is the service of subjugation</t>
    <t s="27">(which has an advantage even over the service of stripping away desires),</t>
    <t s="28">that this service is through the aspect of "male"</t>
    <t s="29">(bent ram's horns),</t>
    <t s="30">"a man's way is to conquer."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the mitzvah of shofar on Rosh Hashanah draws down a new light that renews all of creation, accomplished specifically through the service of Israel, who are G-d's children.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is the mitzvah of the day with the shofar,</t>
    <t s="2">that through the service of the shofar in the two modes of "straightening" and "bending"</t>
    <t s="3">[each of which has a unique advantage]</t>
    <t s="4">they draw down a new light,</t>
    <t s="5">as explained in Iggeret HaKodesh</t>
    <t s="6">that on every Rosh Hashanah a new light is drawn down that never existed before,</t>
    <t s="7">and through this, renewal occurs in the entire order of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="8">even reaching renewal in the externality of the worlds.</t>
    <t s="9">And although the primary renewal on Rosh Hashanah is in the inwardness of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless, through this, renewal occurs also in the externality of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="11">as explained in the Siddur</t>
    <t s="12">in the discourse "L’havin Inyan Teki’at Shofar al pi Kavvanat HaBaal Shem Tov z"l."</t>
    <t s="13">And all this is accomplished through Israel, "a people close to Him,"</t>
    <t s="14">"You are children to Hashem your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="15">as the Maggid explains in Likutei Amarim and Or HaTorah at their beginning, regarding the matter of "Whom He consulted? The souls of the righteous,"</t>
    <t s="16">that the delight He would take in the service of Israel arose before Him,</t>
    <t s="17">and this determined the [primordial] will,</t>
    <t s="18">and from the aspect of the absolute will it was drawn to the revealed will,</t>
    <t s="19">and afterwards it was drawn through the entire order of the chain of descent until this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="20">for specifically through this the intention of "a dwelling place for Him in the lower realms" is completed.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is the meaning of "Say before Me [verses of] Malchuyot so that you will coronate Me over you... and with what? With a shofar,"</t>
    <t s="22">which means the actual blowing of the shofar in deed,</t>
    <t s="23">for "the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,"</t>
    <t s="24">except that included in this</t>
    <t s="25">(in continuation of the beginning of the maamar, "Say before Me... and Shofarot")</t>
    <t s="26">is also the recitation of the verses of Shofarot,</t>
    <t s="27">[and particularly, according to this, one can reconcile our version in the Gemara with the version</t>
    <t s="28">"Say before Me [verses of] Malchuyot so that... Zichronot so that... Shofarot so that..." and the thirteen [shofar blasts] afterwards,</t>
    <t s="29">"and with what? With a shofar."]</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the verse "And on your joyous days... you shall blow with trumpets" refers to the connection of the two halves of a form—G-d and Israel, and the higher and lower parts of each soul—uniting them before G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this verse</t>
    <t s="2">("And on your joyous days... and you shall blow with trumpets...")</t>
    <t s="3">is the continuation and conclusion of the matter preceding it,</t>
    <t s="4">"Make for yourself two trumpets...,"</t>
    <t s="5">and the teaching of the Maggid is known,</t>
    <t s="6">"Two trumpets, two half-forms,"</t>
    <t s="7">meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel are,</t>
    <t s="8">[so to speak,</t>
    <t s="9">and perhaps even without "so to speak",]</t>
    <t s="10">two half-forms.</t>
    <t s="11">From this, the explanation of the verse is understood: "And you shall blow with trumpets... and they shall be for you as a remembrance before your G-d, I am Hashem your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="12">that the matter of Malchuyot</t>
    <t s="13">("I am Hashem your G-d")</t>
    <t s="14">and Zichronot</t>
    <t s="15">("and they shall be for you as a remembrance")</t>
    <t s="16">which is accomplished through "and you shall blow with trumpets,"</t>
    <t s="17">"With trumpets and the sound of the shofar, shout before the King, Hashem"</t>
    <t s="18">[for in the Temple</t>
    <t s="19">("before your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="20">"before the King, Hashem")</t>
    <t s="21">both were present</t>
    <t s="22">(except that the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,</t>
    <t s="23">as explained in the Mishnah),</t>
    <t s="24">and through the "latticed windows, unopenable" that were in the Temple,</t>
    <t s="25">this was drawn</t>
    <t s="26">(as all matters of the Temple)</t>
    <t s="27">also to the outlying areas, even to the entire world.</t>
    <t s="28">And even in the time of exile],</t>
    <t s="29">it is because the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are two half-forms.</t>
    <t s="30">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="31">that the second soul in Israel is literally a part of G-d above,</t>
    <t s="32">and it is known</t>
    <t s="33">that there are two extremes in this.</t>
    <t s="34">For "literally" applies to "a part of G-d above,"</t>
    <t s="35">meaning that the second soul in Israel is a literal part of His very Essence [Atzmus],</t>
    <t s="36">and the Baal Shem Tov's statement is known,</t>
    <t s="37">"When you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp the whole of it,"</t>
    <t s="38">and the word "literally" also indicates the lowest extreme,</t>
    <t s="39">"literally" that which is grasped by the sense of touch.</t>
    <t s="40">And this is what it means that the second soul in Israel is literally a part of G-d above,</t>
    <t s="41">that even when it is clothed in a physical body, literally from the word "touch,"</t>
    <t s="42">even then it is a literal part of His Essence and Being, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="43">one literal [unity] with His Essence [Atzmus],</t>
    <t s="44">and according to the teaching of the Maggid</t>
    <t s="45">(cited above)</t>
    <t s="46">that they are two half-forms.</t>
    <t s="47">And now, since "you are called 'man'"</t>
    <t s="48">on the name "similar to the One above,"</t>
    <t s="49">it is understood that the matter of two half-forms is also within the soul itself.</t>
    <t s="50">For it is known</t>
    <t s="51">that in every soul there are two general levels,</t>
    <t s="52">the part of the soul that is above</t>
    <t s="53">(the aspect of the mazal)</t>
    <t s="54">the "head" of the soul,</t>
    <t s="55">and the part of the soul that is in the body</t>
    <t s="56">(the revealed faculties)</t>
    <t s="57">the "foot" of the soul.</t>
    <t s="58">And these two aspects are the two half-forms within each particular soul.</t>
    <t s="59">And the meaning of "And you shall blow with trumpets... and they shall be for you as a remembrance before your G-d..." is that one must connect his two half-forms</t>
    <t s="60">and place them</t>
    <t s="61">(אַוועקשטעלן זיי)</t>
    <t s="62">before Hashem your G-d,</t>
    <t s="63">and through the connection of these two half-forms</t>
    <t s="64">(head and foot)</t>
    <t s="65">within each particular soul,</t>
    <t s="66">through this the connection of the head and foot of all of Israel is also accomplished, and their elevation before Hashem your G-d,</t>
    <t s="67">"You are standing today"</t>
    <t s="68">(Rosh Hashanah)</t>
    <t s="69">"all of you before Hashem your G-d: your heads... until your woodcutters and water drawers,"</t>
    <t s="70">that all of Israel</t>
    <t s="71">[the "head" of Israel</t>
    <t s="72">("your heads")</t>
    <t s="73">and the "foot" of Israel</t>
    <t s="74">("your woodcutters and water drawers")]</t>
    <t s="75">are connected together and they stand and are elevated before Hashem your G-d,</t>
    <t s="76">and they become one thing with Him, as the verse continues,</t>
    <t s="77">"to pass into the covenant...," for the matter of the covenant is that they become one thing.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
